newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Weak Indian demand, prices seen till December.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Weak Indian demand, prices seen till December.

text.p: Gold demand in India is seen slowing down due to higher supply till December when the wedding season begins, dealers and analysts said on Monday.
Dinesh Parikh, a top jeweller, said that the trade also expected prices to remain weak until next month when improved demand would see it rise.
In Pakistan, traders said gold rates were likely to remain at current levels while Dubai dealers said they hoped India's wedding season and an improved harvest there would boost demand.
Indian traders said long-term gold prospects were good because some buying by investors, moving away from stocks in a depressed market, was expected in December and January.

Gold prices weakened last week with 24 carat gold per 10 grammes falling by three rupees to 4,755 rupees ($133) while prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) fell by 350 rupees to 60,100 rupees in the week to Friday.
Indian markets were closed on Monday for a local holiday.
Last week's weaker tendency was also due to a depreciating dollar against the Indian rupee which made gold imports cheaper resulting in more supply, dealers said.
In Karachci, dealers said major players with a longer term view were switching to the dollar, which has been gaining in international markets against other major currencies.
"Their view is that a strong dollar in the international market could force Pakistan to lower its rupee within the next couple of months," one dealer said.

The dealer, however, said gold prices would not fall sharply because gold consumption by jewellers was rising in the marriage season ahead of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan likely to start in mid-January.
Dealers said 24 carat gold per 10 grammes in Karachi was traded at 5,290 rupees ($131.5).

Dubai gold traders are hoping for a rise in jewellery and bullion sales. The second Indian marriage season, running from mid-November to the end of February, usually sees a strong upturn in bullion and jewellery purchases, much of which is supplied from Dubai where prices are lower than in Bombay.
"We expect good demand from weddings," one Dubai souk (market) trader said.
"An improved economy (in India) and richer farmers after a better harvest will hopefully bring good results to our business."
He was referring to fiscal reforms implemented by India's Central Bank and expectations of a good harvest after strong monsoon rains between June and September.

It is wedding demand, after the Diwali (the Hindu festival of lights) holiday earlier this month, that makes India the world's single largest consumer on gold and Dubai a major re-exporter of the yellow metal.

In line with lower international gold prices, Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT bar) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,204 dirhams ($1,418), down from 5,255 dirhams on November 17.
On the international market, an ounce of gold was last quoted on Saturday at $376.35/85 from the previous Saturday's $380.00/50.
